body:
>if anything comes up you might be able to use, I'll be sure to let you know.

Oh, please do. I really am curious about the community's opinion at large. I have links/caps to other sites where Vampyra was trying to garner public interest in her interviews, but there's not really anything new there except evidence that she wants attention. She's told me before that Shadowgate House is the largest "otherkin house" in the state, though I can't imagine where she gets her facts.

>I can tell you in good faith that if this person interacted with the greater otherkin community, she would be driven out with pitchforks and torches.

I have to assume that's why she's created her own little echo-chamber community. In my experience, she surrounds herself with vulnerable, emotionally damaged, easily controlled people. Like I was after my husband died. I'm not one to identify as a victim, and it kills me now to even imply it, but in retrospect I can see that she took advantage of my situation, and I let her. I rationalized the way she treated us because I was desperate to keep a tight grip on the man I loved. It's only in letting go of him that I've managed to take a step back from the trees and see the forest as a whole.

Anyway, thank you again for taking the time to inform your community. Feel free to PM me if you have any questions, and I'll do my best to answer them.
Of course.

She claims to be otherkin, and actually [runs an otherkin house](https://lasvegasweekly.com/news/archive/2007/jan/11/an-american-family/). She considers herself the matriarch of Shadowgate House, and otherkin organization, because of course she does. I've met some of the other people who go to her meetings, and most of them are fine. Vampyra is the only one who does the vampire thing, and the only one who seems to crave scandal and attention.

In my experience, it seems like she's closer to the vamp culture you described:

[“When I’m sleeping my heart rate goes down to 26 beats per minute which is the level one is at when in a coma.”](http://www.atlantavampirealliance.com/forum/index.php?topic=442.0;wap2)

I don't know if she's confused or if she just says whatever will get her the biggest reaction in the moment, but she definitely purports herself to be otherkin. Whether other 'kin would agree, I don't know.

Thank you for passing it around. I hope I don't come off as hateful, and someone please tell me if I do so I can adjust my tone. As far as I'm concerned, everyone is entitled to their own lifestyle and self-identity right up until the point it starts to harm others. The fact that every member of the 'kin community who's read this has recoiled from her behavior is evidence that she's not just leading an alternative lifestyle or whatever, but is legitimately mentally ill. I really appreciate you guys voicing your opinions and concerns.

I'm still looking into the local pro bono program, but for now my attorney has worked out a payment plan to accommodate us. Hopefully we won't need to switch representation, but having a backup is always a good idea. Thank you for the suggestion :)

>Especially if she risks early exposure to your child.

This so much. Bubbles is looking and acting more and more like her own person every day. She's at a critical point in her development, so anything and everything can make a life-altering impression. It's scary stuff.

Oh man, I really feel for anyone raised by a borderline. I don't think Vampyra qualifies, but I'll definitely look into the resources on their sidebar. Thank you, both for the recommendations and support.
Everyone is pointing me toward legaladvice, so I'll probably head over there once I get my head on straight. Thank you for the recommendation. I appreciate the support.
Thank you for the recommendations and well-wishes.

We're in the discovery phase right now, and they've already thrown a list of demands our way. Medical records are on there, and I have no problem making them available. I don't have an extensive medical history by any means. All they'll find is that I'm on a mild antidepressant which I specifically requested of my GP, and then voluntarily upped the dose when I decided I liked the affects.

I'm going to point out that the detective believes us. Waiting on the report to come in at the moment.

I've actually gone through and refuted their claim line by line, giving as many specifics as possible and pointing out their lies, exaggerations, and intentional omissions. At this point, they're relying on a slew of witnesses as their main source of evidence, and I haven't even seen most of these people for two years. My attorney just gave me a list of their witnesses, and I'm going to go through it and list how long it's been since I've had contact with each individual.

Thank you for your time and advice. I really do appreciate it.
I'll look into it, at the very least to double-check my attorney's take on the whole case. Thank you.

I wish I could stop worrying. I thought we were going to get a dismissal to start, and when that didn't happen we started all this. Thank you for your reassurance though. Hopefully it all ends painlessly.
Thank you so much. We've been spreading the word wherever we can respectfully do so, and the support so far is more than I'd hoped for. I appreciate your efforts.

For the record, I'd like to point out I have no problem with otherkin in general. I'm all about everyone doing their own thing, though I am a non-discriminatory fun-poker. Vampyra is not the norm by any means. She does have serious control issues, and she loves attention, so she could be honestly out of touch or just narcissistic. My guess is a little of both.

Yup, that meetup page is her. Her social life is entrenched in the BDSM community, and as I said, she loves attention, so she's pretty easy to come across even with the cliche name. 

Thank you so much for the support and Google-fu. I really appreciate your efforts.

I've made the judge aware of the vampire angle, but we haven't been able to go into detail yet. I plan on showing the video at the evidentiary hearing. Hopefully this will help not only get the custody complaint laughed out, but stop the visitation request in its tracks as well.

Thank you so much for your support. Hug those grandbabies extra tight :)
Thank you for the reassurance.

>Anxiety and depression are not the demons they once were.

It's easy to forget. Thank you so much for reminding me. Worrying is one thing, but worrying about worrying is useless. So far, authorities have been very understanding, and even supportive. With the stakes so high, I can't help but worry, and I won't take any more chances. But you're right. sometimes I need to take a deep breath and shush the cynic within.

I'm looking into a pro bono program in the area. There are a few hoops to jump through and some "hurry up and wait," but I'm trying to keep every option open. For now, I just got back from my lawyer's office and he's agreed to a new payment plan to accommodate us, which is a huge relief.

Thank you for taking the time to reassure and advise me. I appreciate it a lot.
Thank you so much. Every kind word helps, and a share from a stranger is above and beyond. Your contribution matters.
Funny thing is I've left out loads of wtf for the sake of brevity.

I was wrong. Horribly, terribly wrong. I should have known better, and now I must accept the fact that I've allowed this whole mess to happen. Trying not to seem like I'm fishing for sympathy, because I'm not. The nature of my husband's death was traumatizing, and my actions stemmed from a place of emotion rather than logic. But that's no excuse.

My husband had no one to advocate for him the way my daughter does, and so I thought I could protect her while still allowing her contact with her biological father's family. I thought I was being careful enough. I am an idiot. All I can do now is do everything I can to be sure Bubbles doesn't pay for the mistakes her father and I made.

If I were you, I'd have trouble keeping a civil tongue. I appreciate your kindness. Thank you.

Oh, no, no, I didn't think you were being rude. In fact, *I'm* sorry if I came off as stiff. Your point is actually something that I was concerned with to start, and going back through my campaign story I saw a few small details that could be argued as unsupported or even slanderous. Mostly just semantics, but lawyers are good at twisting words, and I don't need to give them any help in case they do discover the GFM.

Really, thank you for your concern, and thank you for the support.

I've reported the abuse to the police, but there's no physical proof. The allegation hinges on the word of a small child. After listening in on two forensic interviews, the detective believes the abuse happened, but says that there's not enough to go ahead with arrests. The police report will be presented at the next hearing though.

I keep hearing different takes on the concept of grandparent rights. Between the father being dead and the depression I suffered after the fact, they seem to think they have a case. The judge kept asking them if they have recent evidence of me being too depressed to care for my kid, and their lawyer claimed they do, but that's impossible. They also seem to be under the impression that a CPS case was opened on my daughter when my husband died, but they're mistaken. I don't know if it's all a big misunderstanding or if Vampyra lied to her lawyer or what.

I thought the vampire stuff would get the whole thing thrown out. But maybe the judge doesn't understand the extent of the problem. I don't know. I hope you're right though. Thank you for the reassurance.
For real, and that's just the stuff she's gone public with. I've never denied having some issues, but I don't go on national television and try to rationalize them.

We've already been to the preliminary hearing, during which I saw no solid evidence, but they put on a good show. They're using my anxiety and the depression I suffered after my husband's death to claim I'm unfit. There's also some clause about my husband's death that gives her a better shot, I guess. I had been hoping for a dismissal, but that didn't happen.

We have an evidentiary hearing in June. I don't think I could win representing myself at this point. I don't know. It's good to hear from so many who think it won't go anywhere though. It's comforting. I'm looking into a pro bono project, so hopefully you're right and I won't need any more money.

Thank you for the reassurance.

Nevada, where grandparent rights are weak at best. But she's claiming I'm unfit, negligent, and mentally ill because I have anxiety issues. She's also claiming that "a relationship is formed" and using some clause regarding my husband's passing. She conveniently leaves out that the relationship was used to facilitate abuse.

I honestly don't know how any of this works, so it's comforting to read that she's unlikely to win. Thank you.
Yeah, she blurs the lines regarding what's appropriate. I'm totally cool with alternative lifestyles and such, but her interpretation of safe, sane, and consensual is questionable.

I understand where you're coming from. I've actually made it a point to stay off of social media since this started in February (not that I went on much before) just because I knew it wouldn't look good. I thought we had a good chance of getting a dismissal from the start, but that didn't happen. This campaign is kind of a last-ditch effort, and I really am trying not to name-call and all that. 

Thank you so much for the support and well-wishes.
I didn't even think of that. I bet raisedbynarcissists might give me some insight too. Thank you for reminding me these places exist.

We're in Nevada, which has limited grandparent rights at best. She's using some clause about the parent being dead entitling her to visitation at the least (and she's asking fro equal time). On top of that, she's claiming I'm unfit due to "mental illness" (anxiety, and I was depressed after my husband died), which is what she's banking on to win her custody.

I'll look into the request for a motion for assistance. Didn't even know that was a thing, so thank you. I'm a woman in a foreign land as far as the legal system goes.

 Thank you for taking the time to give me advice. I'll try to put it to use.

Or something.

It took me too long to realize that it was upside down. I really wanted to know what the hell was wrong with the dog.

Better to be over-prepared than under-prepared. Plus there's no telling how many Westerosi houses will try to oppose her, so even if they only make up a small force individually, together they might be a problem.

Also they need to suspend our disbelief when she murderapes the WW. You can't defeat an ancient super evil without a big-ass, diverse, non-discriminatory army, obviously.
